title: Stale generation-complete notification: _doneCount never expires, so an old batch fires against a much later drain
description:
Fabio, 2026-08-11, same session as MPI-539 but a different subsystem: 'Toasts are all fucked. It's telling me that the generation is complete, something that I've done ages ago.' Screenshot shows a Windows/Electron OS notification reading 'Generation complete / 2 generations finished' while he was sitting on the LANDING page with Settings open, roughly an hour after the generations in question (app.log has the Krea2 runs at 16:01-16:05Z).

MECHANISM. js/shell/notificationService.js:32 keeps _doneCount, a MODULE-LEVEL counter incremented on every non-cancelled generation:complete. It is only ever flushed by _maybeArmFlush, which requires state.generationQueueCount to read 0. NOTHING EXPIRES IT: there is no timestamp on the count, no staleness gate at fire time, and destroyNotificationService (the only reset) is documented as hot-reload/tests only. So if the queue count does not cleanly reach 0 when a batch ends - which is exactly what a stranded or errored lane produces, and MPI-539's incident produced several - the count simply survives, and the notification fires whenever the count NEXT reaches 0. That can be an unrelated later generation, or a navigation that re-derives the count, an hour on.

The body is built from the surviving count too, so it reports 'N generations finished' for a batch that is no longer the one the user is looking at.

SECOND HALF, NEEDS ITS OWN REPRO BEFORE ANY FIX. Fabio also reported install-notification spam during the agent Pod test runs ('they kept having toasts all over the place saying that this is installed, that is installed'). Not yet reproduced or root-caused. Note for whoever picks it up: the download:complete handler at notificationService.js:~160 already filters !data.modelId, and the MPI-539 reconcile path broadcasts with modelId: null, so that path is NOT the source - do not assume it is. The candidate worth checking first is a model-level download:complete being re-broadcast when the install SSE reconnects and replays, which the MPI-539 recovery path can trigger more than once.

DO NOT FIX BY CLEARING _doneCount ON NAVIGATION. That is the symptom. The count needs either a timestamp checked at fire time, or an owner tied to the batch it belongs to, so that a count belonging to a drained-and-gone batch can never attach itself to a later drain.

SPLIT FROM MPI-539 DELIBERATELY: different module, independent root (a counter with no expiry misfires with or without a Pod), no shared code path with the download-mode engine split.
